description: Governance capacity collapses across climate health finance migration technology and security domains.
Blocs and rival standards fragment global governance capacity.
Crisis pressure produces rapid institutional action but also risks coercion and unequal burden.
Private infrastructure increasingly governs public life without sufficient public accountability.
Technical and expert systems coordinate but democratic accountability remains weak.
Regional capacity grows while global authority remains uneven.
Institutions reform before crisis stress overwhelms cooperation.
Participation accountability representation and public finance improve cooperation.
